According to genetics it's fairly clear, only about one in a thousand isn't simply male or female.

In psychology it's different.

And how so psychologically? I see this thrown around by social 'scientists', saying its psychological. (As if it absolves them from providing any proof)

But you must remember the mind is physical part of our body, so you need physical evidence to prove your gender theories. I have never seen any coherent argument for gender fluidity... much less actual physical studies.

And how so psychologically? I see this thrown around by social 'scientists', saying its psychological.

I'm no psychologist, so I can't answer this question based on anything solid.

Eh. Physical sciences have insufficient ability to comment on the mind at thus far because we don't understand enough about how the mind and the brain and the body work. Right now, we can't make the leap from "thought" to "chemical/electrical pattern in the body" or vice versa; the best we can manage is correlating physical observations with mental experiences, and even then that's iffy.

Tumblr, being a website, is unlikely to have made anything.

The sexual organs you're born with aren't necessarily related to your chromosomes. For example, a woman with complete Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome may genetically be a man. That is among several other conditions that can create a situation, by birth, where genetics and phenotype simply don't match. Similarly, there are a great many people born with ambiguous genitalia.

Additionally, there's overwhelming evidence that gender development (and often identity) is overwhelmingly influenced by a cocktail of hormones -- hormones everyone, male or female, has. Men have some estrogen, and women have some testosterone. Often "pats" -- people who seem to be androgynous in physical characteristics and mannerisms -- have surprisingly even levels of hormones for each sex. And gender identity may well be determined largely in the womb, during which coincidences of hormones could alter the way the brain develops. Transgender individuals, even well before they undergo any treatment, often exhibit brain scans typical of their opposite genetic gender.

Of course, this is all stuff you can google. And probably something they should teach in school. Yes, gender is very fluid. Gender is an evolutionary coincidence, and like all evolutionary traits, it is subject to the whims of nature and proclivities of individuals. Where social conservatives get this idea that gender is hard-and-fast is what, to me, is a complete mystery. It's self-evidently not the case.

Oh Tumblr makes up A LOT of things.

But one must not take the outliers of the population of people and claim that it proves a norm. Thats bad science. Yes there are abnormalities in the womb that can influence or even create abnormal sexualities, hermaphodites, or even androgynous characteristics.

But that doesn't disprove the fact that women and men have hard, across the line gender characteristics that are too high a percentage of people to be mere coincidence.

And no, a woman who occasionally shows male characteristics (or vice versa) is not grounds for something as broad as gender 'fluidity'. Is the fact that there are some small percentage of ppl who are born with an extra limb prove limb 'fluidity'? No, and the science for fluidity is to shaky for it to be in school books for now.

Nobody's claiming that most people with XX chromosomes aren't genetically, physically, and psychologically identified women. And nobody's claiming the same can't be said about XY chromosomes and men.

For the most part, most people identify strongly with one gender or another.

But that doesn't mean there's no fluidity, nor does it mean that any given person is 100% one gender and 0% the other. The idea of gender fluidity isn't that gender doesn't exist. It's that there is some give and take between the genders -- which seems to be the case. At a very basic level, there is gender fluidity insofar as there are tom girls who like baseball and elegant men who, despite being definitely heterosexual men, simply care more about brunch than football.

"Gender fluidity" is simply a term that we use to describe this obvious fact. It isn't a social movement, or a Tumblr meme. It's a word for the obvious.
